clue.text: More appealing modelled attires

indicators.note: modelled means shaped into a new form, so the letters of attires are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothes look nicer when someone shows them off on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' looks like part of the fashion picture but is the anagram signal working on ATTIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier is used loosely of anything more attractive or inviting, a comparative of tasty in the sense of appealing.

clue.text: Pig out, finding this food

parts.note: a pig out in the woods snuffles up this prized underground fungus; pig out also teases the idea of gorging

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig out' reads as gorging, but it is a pig outdoors, hunting the fungus truffle hunters train pigs to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs are traditionally used to sniff out this expensive underground fungus eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Locate model worried about uniform

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: to sit is to model for an artist
ate means worried, as in what's eating you
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A fashion model is anxious about what she must wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To place or position something somewhere is to set it in a location.

clue.text: Flower on top of hill from Dublin?

parts.note: the iris is a garden flower

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of hill, as this is a down clue

explanation.surface: A flower growing on a hilltop near the Irish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital of Ireland, so someone or something from there is an example of being of that nation.

clue.text: Revolutionary vehicle, favourite for special treatment

parts.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries and communists
a car is a vehicle
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's car is everyone's favourite for VIP treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a long crimson carpet for VIPs is the idiom for treating someone as special.

clue.text: Drop police force by choice

indicators.note: by means beside, so the force is placed next to the choice

parts.note: a plum job or role is a choice one, the best going
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A police force falls in public esteem because of a decision it made.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MET is the usual name for London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for falling sharply or steeply, as a price or a bird might.

clue.text: Parking place for taxis to wait is a joke

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a taxi rank is where cabs queue for fares

explanation.surface: Someone finds it funny to park in the space reserved for cabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a practical trick or jest played on someone.

clue.text: Continued, strangely disregarded

indicators.note: strangely tells us the letters of continued are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Something carried on oddly ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: If something goes unseen or unremarked it has been overlooked or ignored.

clue.text: Coward takes advantage of work

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A spineless person exploits the work of others.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is an old word for a timid, feeble person lacking courage.

clue.text: Track round leading lady's houses?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the track encloses the lady

parts.note: to trace is to track or follow
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: Following the star of a show round to her homes.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual queen. The question mark flags that a terrace is a row of houses rather than a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, so it can stand for the houses in it.

clue.text: Inexperienced peacekeepers put to the test

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces, abbreviated UN
tried means tested or put on trial

explanation.surface: Raw peacekeeping troops are tested for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet tested has no track record, which is what being green or inexperienced means.

clue.text: Cancel a Republican circular

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or declare void

explanation.surface: A political party withdraws a leaflet it had sent out to members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular' looks like a noun (a leaflet), but it is the adjective meaning ring-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular is the technical adjective for ring-shaped, as in an annular eclipse.

clue.text: Echo of past of showy defence player

parts.note: flash is informal for ostentatious or showy
a back is a defensive player in football, hockey or rugby

explanation.surface: A flamboyant defender reminds fans of the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden vivid memory of an earlier event is a scene from the past returning to mind.

clue.text: Some magnate's latest electric vehicle

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tycoon's newest product is a battery-powered car, a nod to Elon Musk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesla is the best-known maker of battery cars, and its name stands for one of its cars.

clue.text: Social occasion of first lady and gentry essentially

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of gentry, its middle letters

explanation.surface: A party hosted by the President's wife and the landed classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' looks like the President's wife, but it is Eve of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A party, ball or reception is an example of a planned happening or function.

clue.text: Moved along a course initially twisted and tangled

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of twisted

parts.note: ravelled means tangled or knotted

explanation.surface: Someone moved along a winding path, mixed up and confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it belongs to 'a course', but it works on 'twisted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey along a route is to go or move along it.

clue.text: Standard of behaviour head teacher announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a principal is the head of a school or college

explanation.surface: The headmistress declares the rules of conduct for the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral rule guiding how someone acts is a code or standard of conduct.

clue.text: Fashionable English stage worker lacking in refinement

parts.note: in means fashionable
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A trendy English stagehand who lacks polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage worker' looks like a stagehand, but splits into stage and worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant describes something clumsy or graceless, without polish or style.

clue.text: Promise oddly glum American organised support

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of glum

parts.note: ran means managed or organised
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A miserable American assured people that support had been arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a firm assurance or pledge that something will be done.

clue.text: Drinks finally sozzling girls

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of sozzling

parts.note: lasses are girls, particularly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: Drinks end up getting some young women very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: SOZZLED is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks are served in tumblers or wine vessels, so the containers stand for what is drunk.

clue.text: Think well of a very quiet ramble

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
to rove is to wander or ramble

explanation.surface: Someone likes a nice peaceful walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to regard it favourably.

clue.text: Challenged on interrupting father

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dad is a familiar word for father
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts their dad and is told off for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to challenge them to do something risky.

clue.text: Obstacle in golf, swaying from side to side

parts.note: a rock is an obstacle in one's path
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A golf course hazard makes a player wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obstacle in golf' reads as a golf hazard; 'in' is taken as written and golf gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocking is moving gently back and forth, like a cradle or a boat.

clue.text: Joy of ultimately untrained boat crew maintaining lead at first

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of untrained
maintaining means holding, so the crew keeps another letter within it

parts.note: a rowing eight is a boat crew of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of lead

explanation.surface: The pleasure of a novice rowing crew that held its lead early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight and joy are synonyms for great happiness or pleasure.

clue.text: Gala perhaps that's big in New York?

definitions.meaning: Gala is a popular variety of eating fruit from an orchard
New York is nicknamed the Big ..., so the word is the one that follows big

explanation.surface: A festive gala event is a big hit in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gala' reads as a party; it is the fruit variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Gala is a named cultivar of the common orchard fruit, and the city's nickname puts that fruit after big.

clue.text: Exactly the same in dialect, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected rearrangement of the letters of in and dialect

explanation.surface: Two regional speech forms turn out to match, much to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that match in every detail are indistinguishable, which is the plain sense.

clue.text: Offender not primarily close to centre of power

indicators.note: not primarily means without the first letter

parts.note: a sinner is one who offends against moral law

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer who was not originally near the seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not primarily' drops the first letter, S, from SINNER. The definition is the INNER circle of power.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner circle is the small group closest to a leader, nearest the core of authority.

clue.text: Exercise time, then shower?

parts.note: a shower is a short fall of rain

explanation.surface: A workout followed by a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' suggests a post-workout wash, but it is a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to exercise or practise to build fitness.

clue.text: Puffed up as two ill men with openings gone

indicators.note: openings are the first letters of each word, and gone says they are dropped

explanation.surface: Two sick men have become bloated now that their airways are blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with openings gone' removes the first letter of each of the four words AS, TWO, ILL and MEN, leaving S, WO, LL and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swollen has expanded or bulged, as if inflated with air.

clue.text: Swedish group half-heartedly perform songs; it's mortifying!

indicators.note: half-heartedly removes half of the heart, one of the two middle letters

parts.note: ABBA is the Swedish pop group of Waterloo fame
to sing is to perform songs

explanation.surface: A tribute band singing ABBA hits without enthusiasm is an embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' takes out one of the two middle Bs of ABBA, leaving ABA.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that lowers a person's dignity or humiliates them.

clue.text: Remote southern bank?

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money

explanation.surface: A distant bank in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' means faint or small here, as in a remote or slender chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight possibility is called either remote or slim, so the two adjectives overlap in that sense.

clue.text: Thing to put in order this evening

indicators.note: put in order means arranged, so the letters of thing and to are rearranged

explanation.surface: A household chore to be sorted out later today.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means during the evening or night of the present day.
